# @dsh/ui-panel-resize
English | 中文
> **A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) client plugin.** Installed into a DSH profile, it adds a draggable bott

om
> border to the Web GUI's conversation header.
> Topics: `dsh` · `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness
` · `cordis-plugin` · `dsh-client-plugin`
## The gap it fills
The conversation header (session title + subagent / mode / background-job chips + the 对话 / 轨迹 tabs)

is
sized purely by its content and has **no adjustment entry point at all**: the cursor does not cha

nge at its
bottom border, and there is no way to squeeze or hide it. This plugin turns that border i
nto a draggable grip.
The sidebar's "drag past the minimum width to collapse" used to live here too and was **removed** —

see
Why not the sidebar.
## Interaction
| Action | Result |
| Move the pointer to the header's bottom border | cursor becomes `row-resize` and a small grip appe

ars |
| Drag up | the header shrinks, overflowing content is clipped; floor is **44px** (title row o

nly) |
| Drag more than **40px** above that floor | the grip turns blue and reads "release to collap

se" |
| Release there | the header collapses to an **8px** strip |
| While collapsed: click the stri

p | expands back to the previous height (or the natural one) |
| While collapsed: drag down more tha

n 24px | same as above |
| Drag down | the header grows, up to **160px** above its natural height |
| Double-click the grip | clears the manual height and returns to the natural one |
A pill beside the grip shows the live height (`xx px`) and switches to the hint text once the collap

se
threshold is crossed.
## Tuning (`lib/client.js`)
| Constant | Value | Meaning |

| `HEADER_MIN` | 44 | lowest visible height (keeps the title row, clips the tabs) |
| `HEADER_COLLAP

SE_SLACK` | 40 | how far below that floor counts as "collapse" |
| `HEADER_COLLAPSED` | 8 | strip he

ight while collapsed |
| `HEADER_MAX_GROWTH` | 160 | growth allowed above the natural height |
| `HE

ADER_DRAG_SLOP` | 3 | travel that turns a click into a drag |
| `HEADER_RESTORE_TRAVEL` | 24 | downw
ard travel that expands a collapsed header |
## Implementation
Only **stable DOM hooks** are used: no hashed class names, and no React-managed subtree is mutated.
- The header is located through `[data-conversation-header-leading]`'s parent (fallback: the widest
`header[data-window-drag]`), marked with the plugin's own `data-dsh-panel-resize="header"`, and size

d
through the `--dsh-panel-resize-header-height` custom property (`!important`, overriding the shipp

ed
`min-height:76px`).
- The grip is a `position: fixed` element appended to `document.body`. Its ge

ometry comes **only from the
header's own `getBoundingClientRect()`** — deliberately: the header's p

arent is a slot host that may be
`display: contents` (a zero-size border box), which is how an early

build produced an invisible
`left:0;width:0` grip. The grip straddles the border: about 7px inside

the header (inside the tab row's
own bottom padding) and about 3px below. When a right panel owns it

s own track
(`[data-rightbar-col]` wider than 0) the grip is clipped to the track's left edge.
- The

preference lives in `localStorage['dsh.ui-panel-resize.header']` =
`{"height":number|null,"collapse

d":boolean}`.
- Every node and listener is owned by `ctx.effect()`, so disabling or hot-replacing th

e plugin removes all
of it. One `<style data-plugin="@dsh/ui-panel-resize">` tag carries the rules.
The plugin injects no service (`inject: []`); it is pure DOM chrome.

## Why not the sidebar
The first revision also collapsed the left sidebar when its width drag was released past the minimum

(the
ChatGPT gesture). It was removed because it does not hold up as a feature:
1. **The outcome was already one step away.** `Ctrl+B` and the sidebar's own collapse control both h

ide the
column. The implementation's own fallback path was to synthesize a `Ctrl+B` keypress — when

a gesture's
fallback is a single keystroke, the gesture adds no capability.
2. **It had a cost, not

just zero benefit.** By the shell's contract, collapsing forgets the dragged width
and reopening ret

urns to the default 280px. A previously safe action ("drag the width") became a
destructive one: ove

rshoot once and the column is gone along with the width you just set.
3. **Narrow-window semantics d

iffer.** Below 1024px, `toggleSidebar()` toggles the narrow "expanded over the
centre" state instead

, so the gesture and the shortcut are not equivalent.
4. **It was the only part of this plugin that

had to fight React's drag lifecycle** — intercepting
`pointerup` in the capture phase, `stopPropagat

ion` to stop the host writing its clamped width back,
manually releasing the pointer capture, and re

-asserting the collapse at 280/720ms. The riskiest, least
maintainable code in the package, serving
a duplicate feature.
The header has no equivalent entry point, so it stays.
